passages.title: How can you stay safe during a thunderstorm?
passages.text:
Thunderstorms happen in every part of the world, and they are especially common in summer. Lightning is a giant spark of electricity between the clouds and the ground. It is extremely hot, several times hotter than the surface of the sun, and it often strikes the highest object in an area.

If you are outdoors when a storm comes …
• Go inside a building or a car with a metal roof as quickly as possible.
• Stay away from tall trees, poles and open fields. Never stand under a lone tree.
• If you are swimming, get out of the water immediately.

If you are inside …
• Stay away from windows and doors.
• Don't use electrical equipment that is plugged into the wall, and avoid taking a shower or bath.
• If you are in a car, keep the windows closed and stay in **<u>it</u>** until the storm has passed.

Remember the 30-30 rule: if you hear thunder less than 30 seconds after you see lightning, go inside, and wait 30 minutes after the last thunder before going back outside.
